rationale:
Evidence from the baseline (entityR2A, 60 trials): the robot leaves the track on 39 of 40 development runs. Mean max_error is about 0.060 to 0.063 m, which equals the off-track limit of 0.06 m for this body (tape half-width plus body_width/4 is below 0.06 for any allowed body width, so the limit is effectively fixed at 0.06 m). Progress stalls at 0.13 to 0.28, so the robot runs off the line early in every track. Line-loss events average 2 per run on s-bend and slalom, so the line is lost after the error has already grown past about 4 cm. The 5 sensors cover only +/-2 cm, so the error grows unseen to the edge of the array before any correction. Also, base_speed 1.6 is likely too fast for the bend radius, and kp 1.5 with kd 0.3 is too weak to pull the robot back in time.

Changes: (1) Seven sensors at 10 mm spacing (x = -0.03 to +0.03), so the array sees offsets up to about 4 cm before line loss. Sensor weights are -2 to +2, linear in x, so a unit of offset gives a predictable signal. (2) kp raised from 1.5 to 3.0 for stronger correction. (3) kd raised from 0.3 to 0.5 to damp the faster response. (4) ki stays at 0 because the integral would wind up on the long curves. (5) base_speed lowered from 1.6 to 1.4 so the robot can hold the line through the sharper bends. The finish-time requirement (about 1.5 m/s) is traded for fewer off-track exits, since a completed run is worth far more. (6) Wheel track narrowed from 0.12 to 0.10 m, so each PWM difference gives a higher turn rate. Mass reduced to 0.6 kg and body_length to 0.15 m, which lowers yaw inertia and speeds up the response. body_width stays at 0.12 m, since widening it does not change the off-track limit.

Expected result: fewer line-loss events (target 0 to 1 per run), progress well above 0.5 on s-bend and slalom, and at least some completions on the oval. Hypotheses to test: (a) the wider sensor array removes most line-loss events; (b) the higher kp with lower speed controls the bends without oscillation. Signs of failure: steering_oscillation above about 0.2 means kd or kp is too high; progress stuck near 0.3 with few line losses means the speed is too low for the bends. Next measurements: progress and line_loss_events show whether the array fixes the loss; max_error and steering_oscillation show whether the gains are balanced; completion_time shows the speed margin.
